title: Office
paragraphs: This was back when Rivals were scrambling to boost Shieldfreeden’s approval ratings.
“Father, you’re here.”
Father and the others came to my agency, where I’m running an idol group featuring Filolial-sama and the others. Panda and Elephant are already checking the venue to see if anyone’s set up any traps.

“I didn’t really pay much attention when we passed by in the carriage… but Shieldfreeden’s urban areas really do resemble the big cities of the world I know. The streets look like those in foreign movies, and if it weren’t for the mix of Demi-Humans and Beastmen, there are times I almost forget I’m in a different world.”
“That’s certainly true.”
Compared to Faubrey or Zeltoble, the townscape is a bit of a knockoff, but it certainly has its authentic moments. That’s precisely why I set up my agency here.

Based on my experiences with those pigs who aspired to be Idols, agencies were often established in places like this, so there must have been a reason. After all, there were a few of those pigs who achieved huge success.

Well then, it’s time to show that I’m more capable than Rivals. Let’s leave the weird national politics to the lawmakers—we just need to win the people’s support as Idols! Now that I have no rivals, it’s time to show Father what I’m made of! By the way, the Filolial-sama members—including Yuki-chan and Sakura-chan—should already be rehearsing on stage by now.
“Lord Kitamura, you’ve chosen a rather unusual place as your base, haven’t you?”

Éclair says this as she looks at the building—if you can even call it that—where my agency is located. There were similar stone buildings along the way to Siltvelt, but this one is certainly more modern. That’s because Shieldfreeden has building materials that resemble concrete.
It’s definitely a skyscraper. At night, there are even streetlights illuminated by Magic—it’s practically a makeshift city. Flashy signs have already been put up, too!
“By the way… where are Yuki and the others?”
“Yuki-chan and the others are still practicing, so I’d like you to come up to the office.”
I guided Father and the others up the building’s stairs and led them to the office on the second floor.
“The first floor looked like a carriage parking lot… but the second floor is the office, huh? It kind of feels like a detective’s office for kids or something.”
“This is where we talk to people who want to partner with us in our Idol business.”
“Oh, is that so? Then maybe the third floor?”
I led Father up to the third floor. The room is stacked with all kinds of costumes. There are also various props stored here to match our different performances.
“This is a spare storage room for the stage costumes I made for the Filolial-sama. It doubles as a dressing room, so they can change at any time.”
“Huh… there are instruments here, too.”
“Idols and singing go hand in hand, you know. We need these to prepare a variety of songs.”
“I thought Gaelion-chan was amazing, but Motoyasu-kun is really putting in a lot of effort, too.”
“If you’d like, why don’t you change into a costume and sing with us?”
I’ve even recreated the look of the armor Father wore in the first world. I made it based on my memories, in case it might be used in the Filolial-sama’s musical.
“Well, I’m fine with it… but it’s nice how it feels like a collection of all the things Motoyasu-kun likes.”
“I’m glad to hear that!”
“Oh, so there are wigs too?”
“We have every color imaginable. Some Filolial-samas like to add highlights, and others like to wear colored contact lenses.”
There are a few Filolial-samas like Kuro-chan. That’s part of their individuality, and it’s wonderful.
“Hmm… You really are quite knowledgeable, Motoyasu-kun.”

“I did a lot of different things back in middle and high school. Ah, come to think of it, I switched to my current hairstyle when I started college to change up my image, but I used to have a hairstyle like this.”

I prepare a wig that’s the same color as my natural hair, with slightly longer bangs, and I tie my hair back so it’s not visible from the outside before putting it on. It makes my eyes look a bit darker, but that’s how I used to look back in middle and high school.
“Whoa! What is this!? You seriously look like one of those plain, unassuming protagonists from a gal game where you can’t even see their eyes!?　What’s going on!?”
Father approached me with more excitement than I’ve ever seen before and stared at me intently. Hehe, I get embarrassed when people look at me like that.

“Whoa! So this is what it looked like back then… When I take a close look, I can tell Motoyasu-kun is actually handsome… I see… So that’s the appeal of that kind of protagonist—that they’re actually handsome underneath it all.”
Father is nodding repeatedly, sounding really impressed. It’s been a while since I’ve been complimented like this, so I’m feeling pretty proud of myself.
“Mr. Iwatani, why are you getting so excited just by looking at Mr. Kitamura?”
“Huh? I mean, wouldn’t even Eclair-san be surprised? These days, Motoyasu-kun’s good looks are so well-hidden that it’s hard to tell at a glance, right?”
“True enough. In terms of disguise, Kitamura-sama is quite skilled. If you look closely at his face, you can tell it’s him, but…”
“I suppose only those in the know can really relate to this… It’s a complicated feeling.”
Father muttered, looking slightly flustered.
“I think there’s no doubt he’s become less conspicuous.”
“That’s not quite what I meant… but never mind.”
“We even have school uniforms, you know?”

I’ve even recreated the school uniform from the school I used to attend. I wanted to dress Filolial-sama in the clothes from her school days, so I recreated them based on my memories. The only regret is that the girls’ uniform was worn by a pig.
“At this point, it’s practically cosplay, but when I think of it as the uniform from the school Motoyasu-kun attended, I can’t help but feel moved… I’m actually a little jealous.”
“Most of the students there were pigs, so the uniforms never really looked their best.”

Looking back, it was a pretty creepy place. And even then, my student life there was on the better side—I only lasted three months. I was forced to transfer schools for various reasons. Especially during high school. I never got bored, but it was a hectic youth. So I actually have a few different kinds of school uniforms.
“……I kind of want to visit Japan where Motoyasu-kun was, but I’m afraid people there would just see me as one of the background characters……”
“Mr. Iwatani?”
Éclair tilts her head and addresses Father.
“Father, there’s a pig here, you know? Who are you hoping will take a look at it?”
“Ah, yeah… I guess that’s how it is with Motoyasu. It’s like… a dreamlike world… that slams me back into reality, I suppose.”
“Do you want to fall in love, Mr. Iwatani? I’m sure you have plenty of suitors, but all I can say is… well, I’m sorry, but I can’t really give you any advice on who to fall for.”
“Yeah… it’s a little hard to be pitied. It’s okay, everyone’s here. I just thought Motoyasu-kun’s world would be pretty tough for me.”
It’s a world full of pigs, after all. I definitely don’t want to go back there. My world is here—this world where Filo-tan and Filolial-sama are.
“So, Motoyasu-kun, I get that this is the office, but where are Sakura-chan and the others?　At a nearby venue or something?”
“It’s over here.”

I’ll lead Father down the stairs to the basement of the building. We’ve set up lighting and a stage down there. Since we’re accommodating the Demi-Humans and Beastmen in Shieldfreeden, we made the stairs extra wide—even an elephant could walk down them. By the way, it looks like the pandas are checking guests’ belongings at the entrance. You never know—there might be some scoundrels out there looking to cause trouble for the Idols. The room is intentionally kept a bit dim, and the stage is set up quite high.
“Well then, Father, please wait here for a moment.”
“Uh… I’m starting to feel a little uneasy, but okay.”
I leave Father and the others there and head to the preparation room behind the stage.
“You should project your voice further. Like this—”
It looks like Zou is holding a conductor’s baton and leading the Filolial-sama in some sort of vocal warm-up. Though his voice is low, it resonates like that of an opera singer.
“Whoa!”
“That’s amazing!”
“Like this?”
The Filolial-sama are following along, replicating the vocalizations Zou has instructed them to make.
“That’s it, that’s it. Good job, good job. If you can do that, everyone will be able to sing even better.”
“Yay!”

The audience is already starting to gather, after all. Selling merchandise is an ironclad rule! I gained a lot of popularity with this in the first world, too! It’s only a matter of time before the Top Ten Members of the Filo Fan Club gather in this loop as well.
“Lord Motoyasu! How’s it going? How did the choreography practice with Sakura go?”
Yuki-chan is dancing very rhythmically, sticking perfectly to the choreography I showed her. That dazzling, sparkling atmosphere is truly idol-like.
“Spot on! Count on you again today!”
“Yes, ma’am!”
“Come on, everyone! Father is here! Let’s get ready just as we planned! Showtime is fast approaching!”
And with that, the performance begins. I’ll start playing my instrument from the back of the stage.
“Ah, Naofumi.”

Sakura-chan notices Father and goes over to him. She’s wearing a costume modeled after the one Filo-tan was wearing. Though I feel like it doesn’t quite suit Sakura-chan’s vibe. Let’s just go with it!

And so, accompanied by the music we created, the fun show began with the Filolial-sama singing and dancing. For the main act, Yuki-chan and Sakura-chan start dancing just as we’d rehearsed. Sakura-chan is a bit behind, but we’re not going to let that bother us—we’re prioritizing having fun.
Soon, the Filolial-sama ladies, who had been serving as backup dancers, took turns singing, and the show really started to heat up. The audience happily waved their glow sticks along with the music.
“L・O・V・E. Love!”
The audience joined in on the fan choreography I’d had them learn, and the entire venue became one. Eventually… the hour-long show came to an end.

After the fans’ clapping and cheers died down—clap, clap, clap—the performance ended for the time being, the stage curtain fell, and the audience began to leave. After a short intermission, the show would resume in a few hours.
“What did you think?”
I asked Father and the Éclairs. I think it was a great show.
“Yeah. I think everyone’s singing and dancing were top-notch.”
All right, then. That’s high praise indeed.
“But…”
Father looked slightly troubled, as if choosing his words carefully. Was something wrong?
“Why an underground stage? There don’t seem to be as many people as I expected… though there do seem to be some die-hard fans.”
“Everything starts in a place like this, and this will become a sacred venue for Filolial-sama and the others’ live performances.”
“Hmm…”
Father’s reaction seems a bit lackluster.
“Is that because it’s backed by Motoyasu-kun’s experience?”
“That’s right. We’re drawing inspiration from people like Buta, who was an Idol in Japan before coming to this world.”

Even if we’re using Filo’s concert tour as a reference, I know full well that those shows had to be held in situations where everyone was already aware of the situation. So, starting with shows like this—where those in the know will appreciate them—we’re aiming to expand nationwide. In short, it’s all about cutting our teeth.
“There’s no other way to put it—they’re just underground Idols…”
Father said this in a rather gloomy tone, resting his knees and both hands on the ground. Did I say something wrong?!
“I’m sure they’re trying their best not to lose to Gaelion-chan, but they’re falling short in terms of scale…”
“This is her home turf! The ultimate shortcut to boosting Filolial-sama’s popularity is to gather devoted followers first, then let word of mouth spread her fame! Fan service is key.”
“I’m sure Motoyasu-kun was taking cues from idol-style heroines and handling things well… but I’m starting to feel really anxious.”

Father gave me a suspicious look, as if wondering if I was just cheering her on or providing emotional support. I’d love to cast aside my memories of that pig, but that pig put on a show like this, and it drew a massive crowd! In the end, we secured a massive venue and achieved a huge success! The number of customers here will increase in no time! This is just how it goes at the beginning! Eventually, admission tickets will become highly sought after!
“I don’t really understand the point of a place like this… but is it no good?”
Éclair said, without really understanding.
